title: Platform systems & services — wiki, playbooks, dashboards, and runbooks
author: Ava Patel
content:
Summary:
This page is the canonical eng-platform index for systems and services: operational runbooks, how-tos, dashboards & alerts guidance, retrospective templates, and the near-term roadmap. It consolidates links, ownership, and standards so platform engineers and on-call responders have a single place to find procedures and observability guidance.

Purpose & scope:
- Scope: all Redwood Inference platform systems (control plane services, deployment pipelines, observability stack, common service libraries).
- Audience: platform engineers, SREs, on-call responders, and partner service teams integrating with platform components.
- Goals: reduce time-to-repair, standardize alerts and runbooks, surface roadmap priorities, and make onboarding self-serve.

Owner & contacts:
- Primary owner: eng-platform team (oncall-owner@redwood.ai)
- Pager rotation: platform-oncall (Slack: #oncall-platform)
- Escalation: Level 1 -> oncall -> Level 2 -> service owner -> Level 3 -> eng-platform manager.

How this page is organized (quick links):
1) Systems & services inventory (service name, owner, SLA)
2) How-tos & templates (deployment, onboarding, feature flags)
3) Dashboards & alerting standards (dash naming, alert runbooks, thresholds)
4) Runbooks (playbook per major service)
5) Retrospectives & postmortem templates
6) Roadmap & active initiatives
7) Team wiki & onboarding checklist

1) Systems & services inventory (summary table)
- Service: platform-api | Owner: team-platform-api | SLO: 99.9% p99 latency < 250ms | Pager: platform-oncall
- Service: build-orchestrator | Owner: infra-ci | SLO: 99.5% availability | Pager: infra-oncall
- Service: model-router | Owner: serving-runtime | SLO: 99.9% request success | Pager: runtime-oncall

(For a full CSV export, see the "platform-service-inventory" attachment.)

2) How-tos & templates
- Deploying a service (short procedure):
  1. Ensure tests pass in CI: `ci/run-tests.sh --service $SERVICE`
  2. Bump version in chart: `repo/charts/$SERVICE/Chart.yaml`
  3. Open canary rollout via `kubectl apply -f canary-$SERVICE.yaml` and monitor `/dashboards/$SERVICE/canary`
  4. After 10-15 minutes with stable metrics, promote to stable: `kubectl apply -f stable-$SERVICE.yaml`
  5. Update release notes and notify #deployments.
- Creating a new dashboard: use the grafana-template `grafana/templates/platform-service.json` and populate variables: service_name, team, environment. Save with name: `PLATFORM / <service> / Overview`.
- Feature flag rollout: use LaunchDarkly section `ld/platform-flags` and follow staged rollout 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with metrics gated at each step.

3) Dashboards & alerting standards
- Dashboard naming convention: `PLATFORM / <service> / <view>` (examples: PLATFORM / model-router / Overview, PLATFORM / model-router / Latency)
- Core panels every overview dashboard must include:
  - Request rate (rps)
  - p50/p95/p99 latency (ms)
  - Error rate (5m) and 1h trend
  - Resource saturation (GPU/CPU/memory)
  - Queue depth / backlog (if applicable)
- Alert taxonomy (examples):
  - SEV-1: service down / sustained 500 errors > 2 minutes OR 5xx rate > 10% for 5 minutes
  - SEV-2: latency degradation p99 > SLO * 1.5 for 10 minutes
  - SEV-3: non-critical infra warning (disk usage > 85% on non-prod)

Alert rule sample (Prometheus-style, example):
``
ALERT Platform_High_5xx_Rate
  IF sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="model-router",status=~"5.."}[5m]))
     / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="model-router"}[5m])) > 0.10
  FOR 5m
  LABELS { severity = "page" }
  ANNOTATIONS { summary = "model-router 5xx rate > 10%", runbook = "/runbooks/model-router-5xx" }
``

Alert runbook guidance (short):
1. Confirm the alert in Grafana/Prometheus and Slack channel alerting.
2. Check the Overview dashboard for correlated signals (latency, CPU/GPU).
3. If 5xx spike, tail application logs: `stern model-router -n prod` and grep for exception traces.
4. If rollout-caused, revert canary: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/model-router -n prod`.
5. If infrastructure, open a ticket and escalate to infra-oncall.

4) Runbooks (index and example)
- Runbook index: `/runbooks/platform-api`, `/runbooks/build-orchestrator`, `/runbooks/model-router`, `/runbooks/grafana`
- Example runbook: model-router 5xx spike (summary):
  - Trigger conditions: SEV-1 or SEV-2 5xx/latency thresholds
  - Immediate actions:
    1. Page oncall and allocate primary/secondary.
    2. Post initial triage in incident channel with incident key and timeline.
    3. Check recent deploys: `git log -n 5 --pretty=oneline` for model-router.
    4. If deploy in last 30m, roll back the deploy and observe.
  - Diagnosis checklist:
    - Are model weights failing to load (OOM)? Check pod events and logs.
    - Is downstream storage responding? Run `curl -sS https://status.internal/storage`
    - Any config/feature-flag changes in the last hour?
  - Mitigations:
    - Scale up replicas temporarily: `kubectl scale deploy model-router --replicas=6 -n prod`
    - If OOM, increase container memory or switch to smaller batch size.
  - Post-incident: run retrospective template (see section 5).

5) Retrospectives & postmortem template
- Required for all Sev-1 incidents; recommended for Sev-2.
- Template headings (copy into a new doc):
  - Summary (1-2 sentences)
  - Impact (customers, internal systems, pages)
  - Timeline (bulleted minute-level timeline)
  - Root cause analysis (why this happened)
  - Corrective actions (owner, ETA, verifier)
  - Detection & monitoring improvements (dashboards/alerts to create/change)
  - Communication notes (customer messages, status page updates)

6) Roadmap & active initiatives (next 6 months)
- Q2 2026 priorities:
  - Observability consolidation: migrate dashboards to unified Grafana folders and standardize templates (owner: eng-platform, ETA: 2026-04-15).
  - Alert rationalization: reduce noisy alerts by 40% and add SLA-based SLO monitors (owner: eng-sre, ETA: 2026-05-01).
  - Runbook automation: add a Slack action to run common mitigations (scale, rollback) as approved playbook steps (owner: eng-platform, ETA: 2026-06-01).
  - Onboarding flow: new platform engineer checklist automations in Confluence + 1:1 buddy pairing (owner: people-ops + eng-platform, ETA: 2026-04-01).

7) Team wiki & onboarding checklist
- First week checklist:
  1. Access: request access to GCP project `redwood-platform-prod` and Grafana folder `PLATFORM`.
  2. Read the runbook index and subscribe to platform-oncall rota.
  3. Pair with oncall buddy for a shadow shift.
- Useful links:
  - Dashboard root: /grafana/folders/PLATFORM
  - Runbook index: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
  - CI/CD pipelines: /concourse/pipelines/platform

Appendix: templates and artifacts
- Grafana dashboard template path: `infra/grafana/templates/platform-service.json`
- Prometheus alert templates: `infra/monitoring/alerts/platform.rules`
- Runbook template: copy `/confluence/eng-platform/templates/runbook-template.md`

Change log:
- 2026-01-20 (Ava Patel): initial published playbook and index.
- 2026-03-01 (Ava Patel): added roadmap priorities and runbook automation section.

Ownership & review cadence:
- Owner: eng-platform (doc owner).
- Quarterly review required before each calendar quarter (task assigned to doc owner 30 days before quarter start).

If you find missing services or stale dashboards, file a PR against the service-inventory CSV or open a ticket in the `#platform-docs` Slack channel with the tag `doc-update`.
